title: Heavier-sin repentance must be perfectly practical; lighter cannot be—Baron of Aberdeen
source_text: X. Praeterea poenitentia quae necessaria est, ut peccata graviora homini condonentur, debet esse perfecte practica, hoc est, exire debet in realem & actualem, ab omnibus ejusmodi peccatis cessationem. Nam si quis uno aut altero hujus generis peccato relicto, in alia subinde labatur, is neque gratiam in hac vita, nec gloriam in vita futura consequi poterit. Nam qui talia faciunt regnum Dei non possidebunt, ut pluribus in locis repetit Apostolus. Contra vero poenitentia ad peccatorum leviorum remissionem requisita, nec est, nec esse potest perfecte practica, quoad ejus generis peccata. Nam nemo sine ejusmodi peccatis vivere potest: & per consequens non periclitatur piorum salus, etsi ante finem vitae, non possint hoc peccati genus in totum effugere, ut recte observat Robertus Baronius Abredonensis in Scotiae Academia Professor. Disput. Theologica de peccato Mortali & veniali part. 1. sect. 6. num. 11. & 12.
pass_a_gloss: Moreover the repentance necessary for heavier sins to be pardoned to a man must be perfectly practical—that is, it must issue in a real and actual cessation from all sins of that kind. For if someone, having left one or another sin of this kind, subsequently falls into others, he will be able to obtain neither grace in this life nor glory in the life to come. For those who do such things will not possess the kingdom of God, as the Apostle repeats in many places. But on the contrary, the repentance required for remission of lighter sins neither is nor can be perfectly practical with respect to sins of that kind. For no one can live without sins of that sort; and consequently the salvation of the pious is not endangered even if before the end of life they cannot wholly escape this kind of sin—as Robert Baron of Aberdeen, Professor in the Academy of Scotland, rightly observes (Theological Disputation on mortal and venial sin, part 1, sect. 6, nos. 11–12).
pass_b_english: Heavier pardon demands perfectly practical repentance—real cessation, or no grace/glory.
Lighter faults cannot be perfectly fled in this life; pious salvation is not thereby lost (Baron).

choices.why: Must issue in actual cessation from heavier sins.
